chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who have faith.
But [He granted authority] over those who take him as their guardian and disobey His command.

key_terms.يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُمْ: Those who take him as guardian/ally

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for Satan having authority over believers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a) clarification that Satan’s *sultan* (authority/power) is not inherent or absolute but contingent upon human *ikhtiyar* (free will), distinguishing between those who voluntarily submit to his whispers and those who remain steadfast. This hadith reinforces the Shia theological principle of *Adl* (Divine Justice) by showing that spiritual bondage is a result of choice rather than predestination, thereby preserving human agency in the cosmic struggle between good and evil.
